title: Bekhorot 8
description: A baraita on how creatures mate, give birth and lay eggs, its list of gestation periods matched to trees, the snake’s seven years derived from its curse, and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Ḥananya’s contest of riddles with the elders of Athens.
topics: 🐬 The dulfanin, “sons of the sea,” and which creatures give birth and which lay eggs
🥚 Day births and night births: Rav Mari son of Rav Kahana on an egg found on a Festival morning
🐍 Face to face: fish, humans and the snake, “because the Divine Presence spoke with them”
🌳 Gestation periods and the trees that match them, from the chicken’s 21 days to the viper’s 70 years
📜 “Cursed are you from among all animals”: why the snake carries for seven years
🏛️ The emperor sends Rabbi Yehoshua ben Ḥananya to defeat the sixty elders of Athens
❓ Riddles and retorts: the peg in the wall, the mule’s note, the salt that spoils, the house in the air

a1.he: הַדּוֹלְפָנִין פָּרִין וְרָבִין כִּבְנֵי אָדָם. מַאי דּוֹלְפָנִין? אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: בְּנֵי יַמָּא.

a2.he: כֹּל שֶׁבֵּיצָיו מִבַּחוּץ — מוֹלִיד, וְכֹל שֶׁבִּפְנִים — מֵטִיל בֵּיצִים.

a3.he: אִינִי? וְהָאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: אֲוָוז וַאֲוָוז בָּר כִּלְאַיִם זֶה בָּזֶה, וְהָוֵינַן בָּהּ: מַאי טַעְמָא? אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: זֶה בֵּיצָיו מִבַּחוּץ, וְזֶה בֵּיצָיו מִבִּפְנִים, וְתַרְוַיְיהוּ מְטִילֵי בֵּיצִים!

a4.he: אֶלָּא, כֹּל שֶׁזַּכְרוּתוֹ מִבַּחוּץ — מוֹלִיד, מִבִּפְנִים — מֵטִיל בֵּיצִים.

a5.he: כֹּל שֶׁתַּשְׁמִישׁוֹ בַּיּוֹם — יוֹלֵד בַּיּוֹם, בַּלַּיְלָה — יוֹלֵד בַּלַּיְלָה, כֹּל שֶׁתַּשְׁמִישׁוֹ בֵּין בַּיּוֹם בֵּין בַּלַּיְלָה — יוֹלֵד בֵּין בַּיּוֹם בֵּין בַּלַּיְלָה.

a6.he: תַּשְׁמִישׁוֹ בַּיּוֹם יוֹלֵד בַּיּוֹם — תַּרְנְגוֹל, בַּלַּיְלָה יוֹלֵד בַּלַּיְלָה — עֲטַלֵּף, תַּשְׁמִישׁוֹ בֵּין בַּיּוֹם בֵּין בַּלַּיְלָה יוֹלֵד בֵּין בַּיּוֹם בֵּין בַּלַּיְלָה — אָדָם וְכֹל דְּדָמֵי לֵיהּ.

a7.he: לְמַאי נָפְקָא מִינַּהּ? לְכִדְרַב מָרִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא, דְּאָמַר רַב מָרִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא: בָּדַק בְּקִינָּה שֶׁל תַּרְנְגוֹלִין מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב וְלֹא מָצָא בָּהּ בֵּיצָה, וּלְמָחָר הִשְׁכִּים וּמָצָא בָהּ בֵּיצָה — מוּתֶּרֶת בַּאֲכִילָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב, אֵימַר: לֹא בָּדַק יָפֶה.

a8.he: וַהֲלֹא בָּדַק יָפֶה! אֵימַר: יָצְתָה רוּבָּהּ וְחָזְרָה הֲוָה, וְכִדְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בֵּיצָה שֶׁיָּצְתָה רוּבָּהּ מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב וְחוֹזֶרֶת — מְוֻתֶּרֶת לְאוֹכְלָהּ בְּיוֹם טוֹב.

a9.he: כֹּל שֶׁתַּשְׁמִישׁוֹ וְעִיבּוּרוֹ שָׁוֶה — יוֹלְדִים וּמְגַדְּלִים זֶה מִזֶּה. הַכֹּל מְשַׁמְּשִׁין פָּנִים כְּנֶגֶד עוֹרֶף, חוּץ מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה שֶׁמְּשַׁמְּשִׁין פָּנִים כְּנֶגֶד פָּנִים, וְאֵלּוּ הֵן: דָּג, וְאָדָם, וְנָחָשׁ.

a10.he: וּמַאי שְׁנָא הָנֵי תְּלָתָא? כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמְרִי בְּמַעְרְבָא: הוֹאִיל וְדִיבְּרָה עִמָּהֶם שְׁכִינָה.

a12.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: תַּרְנְגוֹלֶת — לְעֶשְׂרִים וְאֶחָד יוֹם, וּכְנֶגְדָּהּ בָּאִילָן — לוּז, כֶּלֶב — לַחֲמִשִּׁים יוֹם, וּכְנֶגְדּוֹ בָּאִילָן — תְּאֵינָה, חָתוּל — לַחֲמִשִּׁים וּשְׁנַיִם יוֹם, וּכְנֶגְדּוֹ בָּאִילָן — תּוּת, חֲזִיר — לְשִׁשִּׁים יוֹם, כְּנֶגְדּוֹ בָּאִילָן — תַּפּוּחַ, שׁוּעָל וְכׇל מִינֵי שְׁרָצִים — שִׁשָּׁה חֳדָשִׁים, וּכְנֶגְדָּם בָּאִילָן — תְּבוּאָה.

a13.he: בְּהֵמָה דַּקָּה טְהוֹרָה — לַחֲמִשָּׁה חֳדָשִׁים, וּכְנֶגְדָּן בָּאִילָן — גֶּפֶן. בְּהֵמָה גַּסָּה טְמֵאָה — לִשְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חוֹדֶשׁ, וּכְנֶגְדּוֹ בָּאִילָן — דֶּקֶל. טְהוֹרָה — לְתִשְׁעָה חֳדָשִׁים, וּכְנֶגְדָּהּ בָּאִילָן — זַיִת. הַזְּאֵב וְהָאֲרִי וְהַדּוֹב וְהַנָּמֵר וְהַבַּרְדְּלָס וְהַפִּיל וְהַקּוֹף וְהַקִּיפוֹף — לְשָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים, וּכְנֶגְדָּן בָּאִילָן — בְּנוֹת שׁוּחַ.

a14.he: אֶפְעֶה לְשִׁבְעִים שָׁנָה, וּכְנֶגְדּוֹ בָּאִילָן — חָרוּב. חָרוּב זֶה, מִשְּׁעַת נְטִיעָתוֹ עַד שְׁעַת גְּמַר פֵּירוֹתָיו — שִׁבְעִים שָׁנָה, וִימֵי עִיבּוּרוֹ שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים. נָחָשׁ לְשֶׁבַע שָׁנִים, וּלְאוֹתוֹ רָשָׁע לֹא מָצִינוּ חָבֵר. וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: מוֹכְסָסִים.

a15.he: מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי? אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב, וּמָטוּ בָּהּ מִשּׁוּם דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן חֲנַנְיָא, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״אָרוּר אַתָּה מִכׇּל הַבְּהֵמָה וּמִכֹּל חַיַּת הַשָּׂדֶה״. אִם מִבְּהֵמָה נִתְקַלְּלָה, מֵחַיָּה לֹא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן?

a16.he: אֶלָּא, לוֹמַר לָךְ: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁנִּתְקַלְּלָה הַבְּהֵמָה מֵחַיָּה, אֶחָד לְשִׁבְעָה, וּמַאי נִיהוּ? חֲמוֹר מֵחָתוּל, כָּךְ נִתְקַלֵּל הוּא מִבְּהֵמָה, אַחַת לְשֶׁבַע, דְּהָוֵה לֵיהּ שַׁב שְׁנֵי.

a17.he: אֵימָא: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁנִּתְקַלְּלָה חַיָּה מִבְּהֵמָה, אַחַת לְשָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים, וּמַאי נִיהוּ? אֲרִי מֵחֲמוֹר, כָּךְ נִתְקַלֵּל הוּא מֵחַיָּה אַחַת לְשָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים, דְּהָוֵה לֵיהּ תֵּשַׁע שָׁנִים.

b1.he: מִי כְּתִיב ״מִכׇּל הַחַיָּה וּמִכׇּל הַבְּהֵמָה״? ״מִכׇּל הַבְּהֵמָה וּמִכֹּל הַחַיָּה״ כְּתִיב! אָרוּר הוּא מִבְּהֵמָה שֶׁנִּתְקַלְּלָה מֵחַיָּה.

b2.he: וְאֵימָא: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁנִּתְקַלְּלָה בְּהֵמָה מֵחַיָּה אֶחָד לְשָׁלֹשׁ, וּמַאי נִיהוּ? עֵז מֵחָתוּל, כָּךְ נִתְקַלֵּל הוּא מִבְּהֵמָה אֶחָד לְשָׁלֹשׁ, דְּהָוֵה לֵיהּ חֲמֵיסַר יַרְחֵי!

b3.he: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: ״מִכׇּל הַבְּהֵמָה״ כְּתִיב. אִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא: קְלָלָה הוּא, קְלָלָה שְׁדִי עִילָּוֵיהּ.

b4.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ קֵיסָר לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן חֲנַנְיָה: נָחָשׁ לְכַמָּה מִיעַבַּר וּמוֹלֵיד? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לְשַׁב שְׁנֵי. וְהָא סָבֵי דְּבֵי אַתּוּנָא אַרְבְּעִינְהוּ, וְאוֹלִיד לִתְלָת! הָנְהוּ מִיעַבְּרִי הֲווֹ מֵעִיקָּרָא אַרְבַּע. וְהָא קָמְשַׁמְּשִׁי שַׁמּוֹשֵׁי! אִינְהוּ נָמֵי מְשַׁמְּשִׁי כְּאָדָם.

b5.he: וְהָא חַכִּימֵי אִינְהוּ? אֲנַן חֲכִימִינַן מִינַּיְיהוּ. אִי חֲכִימַתְּ, זִיל זַכִּינְהוּ וְאַיְתִינְהוּ לִי! אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כַּמָּה הָווּ? שִׁיתִּין גַּבְרֵי.

b6.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: עֲבֵיד לִי סְפִינְתָּא דְּאִית בַּהּ שִׁיתִּין בָּתֵּי, וְכֹל בֵּיתָא אִית בַּהּ שִׁיתִּין בִּיסְתַּרְקֵי. עֲבַד לֵיהּ. כִּי מְטָא לְהָתָם לְבֵי טַבָּחָא, אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ לְהָהוּא גַּבְרָא דְּקָא פָשֵׁיט חֵיוְתָא. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: רֵישָׁךְ לְזַבּוֹנֵי? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִין. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בְּכַמָּה? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בְּפַלְגָא דְּזוּזָא. יְהַב לֵיהּ.

b7.he: לְסוֹף, אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא רֵישָׁא דְּחֵיוְתָא אֲמַרִי לָךְ? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִי בָּעֵית דְּאֶשְׁבְּקָךְ סַגִּי אַחְוִי לִי פִּיתְחָא דְּבֵי אַתּוּנָא. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִסְתְּפֵינָא דְּכֹל דְּמַחְוֵי קָטְלִי לֵיהּ. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: דְּרִי כְּרִיכָא דִּקְנֵיא, וְכִי מָטֵית לְהָתָם זִקְפֵהּ כְּמַאן דְּקָא מִתְּפַח.

b8.he: אַשְׁכַּח דַּרְבְּנָאֵי מִגַּוַּאי וְדַרְבְּנָאֵי מִבָּרַאי, דְּאִי חָזוּ כַּרְעָא דְּעָיְילָא — קָטְלִי לְהוּ לְבָרַאי, וּדְנָפְקָא — קָטְלִי לְהוּ לְגַוַּאי.

b9.he: אַפְכֵהּ לְסַנְדָּלֵיהּ — קָטְלִי לְהוּ לְגַוָּאֵי, אַפְכֵהּ לְסַנְדָּלֵיהּ — קָטְלִי לְהוּ לְכוּלְּהוּ.

b10.he: אַשְׁכַּח יָנוֹקֵי מִלְּעֵיל, סָבֵי מִלְּתַחַת. אֲמַר: אִי יָהֵיבְנָא שְׁלָמָא לְהָנֵי, קָטְלִי לִי הָנֵי, סָבְרִי: אֲנַן עֲדִיפִינַן, דַּאֲנַן קַשִּׁינַן טְפֵי וְאִינְהוּ דַּרְדַּקֵּי.

b11.he: אֲמַר: שְׁלָמָא לְכוּ. אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: מַאי עֲבִידְתָּיךְ? אֲמַר לְהוּ: אֲנָא חַכִּימָא דִיהוּדָאֵי אֲנָא, בָּעֵינָא לְמִיגְמַר חֻכְמְתָא מִינַּיְיכוּ. אִי הָכִי, נִיבְעֵי לָךְ! אֲמַר לְהוּ: לְחַיֵּי, אִי זָכֵיתוּ — כֹּל דְּבָעֵיתוּ עֲבִידוּ בִּי, וְאִי זָכֵינָא בְּכוּ — אִיכְלוּ גַּבַּאי בִּסְפִינְתָּא.

b12.he: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: הַהוּא גַּבְרָא דְּאָזֵיל וּבָעֵי אִתְּתָא וְלָא יָהֲבוּ לֵיהּ, מַאי חֲזֵי לֵיהּ דְּאָזֵיל הֵיכָא דְּמִדְּלוּ מִינָּיהּ? שְׁקַל סִיכְּתָא, דָּצַהּ לְתַתַּאי — לָא עָאל, לְעִילַּאי — עָאל. אֲמַר: הַאי נָמֵי מִיתְרְמֵי בַּת מַזָּלֵיהּ.

b13.he: גַּבְרָא דְּאוֹזֵיף וְטָרֵיף, מַאי חֲזָא דַּהֲדַר אוֹזֵיף? אֲמַר לְהוּ: גַּבְרָא אֲזַל לְאַגְמָא, קְטַל קַמָּא טוּנָא וְלָא מָצֵי בֵּיהּ, קָטֵיל וּמַנַּח עִילָּוֵיהּ, עַד (דְּאִיתְרְמִי) [דְּמִיתְרְמֵי] אִינִישׁ מַדְלֵי לֵיהּ.

b14.he: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: אֵימָא לַן מִילֵּי דִּבְדִיאִי! אֲמַר לְהוּ: הֲוָה הַהִוא כּוּדַנְיְתָא דִּילִידָא, וַהֲוָה תְּלֵי לֵיהּ פִּיתְקָא, וּכְתַב בֵּיהּ דְּמַסֵּיק בְּבֵי אַבָּא מְאָה אַלְפָּא זוּזֵי. אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: וְכוּדַנְיְתָא מִי יָלְדָה? אֲמַר לְהוּ: (הֵי נִיהוּ) [הָנֵי נִינְהוּ] מִילֵּי דִבְדִיאִי.

b15.he: מִילְחָא כִּי סָרְיָא, בְּמַאי מָלְחִי לַהּ? אֲמַר לְהוּ: בְּסִילְתָּא דְכוּדַנְיְתָא. וּמִי אִיכָּא סִילְתָּא לְכוּדַנְתָּא? וּמִילְחָא מִי סְרֵי?

b16.he: בְּנִי לַן בֵּיתָא בַּאֲוִירָא דְּעָלְמָא! אָמַר שֵׁם, תְּלָא בֵּין רְקִיעָא לְאַרְעָא. אֲמַר לְהוּ: אַסִּיקוּ לִי לִיבְנֵי וְטִינָא. מְצִיעֲתֵיהּ דְּעָלְמָא הֵיכָא? זַקְפַהּ לְאֶצְבַּעְתֵּיהּ, אֲמַר לְהוּ: הָכָא. אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: וּמִי יֵימַר? אַיְיתוֹ אַשְׁלֵי וּמְשַׁחוּ.

b17.he: אִית לַן בֵּירָא בְּדַבְרָא, עַיְילֵאּ לְמָתָא! אֲמַר לְהוּ: אַפְשִׁילוּ לִי חַבְלֵי מִפָּארֵי וַאֲעַיְּילֵיהּ. אִית לַן רִיחְיָא דִּתְבִירָא, חַיְּיטַיהּ. אֲמַר: כְּרוּכוּ לִי מִינַּיהּ גַּרְדֵי וְאִיחַיְּיטַיהּ.

b18.he: מְשָׁרָא דְּסַכִּינֵי בְּמַאי קָטְלִי? בְּקַרְנָא דַּחֲמָרָא. וּמִי אִיכָּא קַרְנָא לַחֲמָרָא? וּמִי אִיכָּא מְשָׁרָא דְּסַכִּינֵי?

b19.he: אַיְיתוֹ לֵיהּ תְּרֵי בֵּיעֵי, אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: הֵי דְּזַגְתָּא אוּכַּמְתִּי וְהֵי דְּזַגְתָּא חִיוַּורְתִּי? אַיְיתִי לְהוּ אִיהוּ תְּרֵי גְּבִינֵי, אֲמַר לְהוּ: הֵי דְּעִיזָּא אוּכַּמְתִּי וְהֵי דְּעִיזָּא חִיוַּורְתִּי?

b20.he: וַרְצוּצָא דְּמִית, מֵהֵיכָא נָפֵיק רוּחֵיהּ? מֵהֵיכָא דְּעָל נְפַק. אַחְוִי לַן מָנָא דְּלָא שָׁוֵי חֲבִילֵיהּ! אַיְיתִי (כֹּל חַד וְחַד) בּוּדְיָא, פַּשְׁטֵיהּ. לָא הֲוָה עָיֵיל בְּתַרְעָא. אֲמַר לְהוּ: אַיְיתוֹ מָרֵי סִיתְרוּהּ. הַיְינוּ מָנָא דְּלָא שָׁוֵי חֲבִילֵיהּ.

b21.he: אַיְתִינְהוּ כֹּל חַד וְחַד, כִּי חָזֵי שִׁיתִּין בִּיסְתַּרְקֵי, אָמַר: כּוּלְּהוּ חַבְרַאי לְהָכָא אָתוּ. אֲמַר לֵיהּ לְסָפוֹנָא: שְׁרִי סְפִינְתָּךְ. בַּהֲדֵי דְּקָאָתוּ שְׁקַל עַפְרָא מֵעַפְרַיְיהוּ.

messages.text: 8a

Continued from 7b: a baraita taught that a non-kosher fish spawns live young while a kosher fish lays eggs, that every creature that gives birth nurses its young, and that every egg-layer gathers food for its young, except the bat. The baraita continues.
Gemara
The dulfanin reproduce like people.

notes.dh: ה"ג הדולפנין פרים ורבים מבני אדם
notes.he: שאם בא אדם עליהם מתעברות הימנו:
notes.en: This is the reading: the dulfanin reproduce from people [Rashi reads “from people,” where the printed Gemara and the English have “like people”]: that if a man has relations with them, they conceive from him.

notes.he: כן גירסת הקונטרס וכן מוכח בתוספתא [פ"א] יולדין ומגדלין מבני אדם:
notes.en: The dulfanin reproduce from people: this is the reading of the Kuntres [Rashi], and so it is evident in the Tosefta (chapter 1): “they bear and raise young from people.”

messages.text: What are dulfanin?
They are creatures that are called sons of the sea.

notes.he: דגים יש בים שחציין צורת אדם וחציין צורת דג ובלע"ז שריינ"א:
notes.en: Sons of the sea: there are fish in the sea that are half in the form of a person and half in the form of a fish. (Rashi adds an Old French gloss.)

notes.he: אדם של ים. כל שביציו מבחוץ חוץ ממעיו כגון בהמה שביצי' חוץ מגופה מוליד נקבתו מולדת:
notes.en: Rav Yehuda said: Sons of the sea: a person of the sea. Any whose testicles are outside, outside its belly, such as a domestic animal whose testicles are outside its body: its female gives birth.

messages.text: In the case of any male animal whose testicles are external, the female gives birth to live offspring, and in the case of any male animal whose testicles are internal, the female lays eggs.

notes.he: מין שביצי הזכר כגון חיה ובהמה מבחוץ מוליד עובר ממש:
notes.en: Any species whose male’s testicles are external, such as wild and domestic animals, gives birth to an actual fetus.

notes.he: מין שביצי זכר מבפנים מטילה הנקיבה ביצים:
notes.en: And any species whose male’s testicles are internal: the female lays eggs.

notes.he: כל שביציו של זכר מבפנים כגון עופות נקבתו מטיל' ביצים:
notes.en: Any whose male’s testicles are inside, such as birds: its female lays eggs.

messages.text: Is that so? But doesn’t Shmuel say:
messages.quote: whose testicles are external, the female gives birth

messages.text: A domestic goose and a wild goose are considered diverse kinds, and one may not mate them with each other.

notes.he: של ישוב ואווז של בר כלאים להרביע לפי שאין הזכרים דומים דזה ביציו מבחוץ וזה ביציו מבפנים:
notes.en: A goose: a domestic goose and a wild goose are diverse kinds with regard to mating them, since the males are not alike: this one’s testicles are external and that one’s are internal.

notes.he: כלאים זה בזה לענין הנהגה:
notes.en: Diverse kinds with each other: with regard to driving them together.

messages.text: And we discussed it: What is the reason?
In the case of this one, the male wild goose, its testicles are external, and in the case of that one, the domestic goose, its testicles are internal.
And yet both geese lay eggs. Evidently, the fact that the male’s testicles are external does not prove that the female gives birth.
Rather, the baraita must mean the following: With regard to any animal whose male reproductive organ is external, the female gives birth,

notes.he: הגיד ואווז בר זכרותו מבפנים:
notes.en: Its male organ: the member. And the wild goose’s male organ is internal.

notes.he: אלא שזכרותו מבחוץ גידו מוליד:
notes.en: Rather, whose male organ is outside, its member: [its female] gives birth.

messages.text: and in the case of any male animal whose reproductive organ is internal, the female lays eggs. Although the testicles of the male wild goose are external, its reproductive organ is internal.

notes.he: זכרותו (מפנים) [מבפנים] מטיל ביצים ואווז בר נמי אע"ג דביציו מבחוץ זכרותו גידו מבפנים הוא (היה) [ומשו"ה] מטיל ביצים:
notes.en: Whose male organ is inside lays eggs. And the wild goose too, although its testicles are outside, its male organ, its member, is inside, and that is why it lays eggs.

messages.text: Any species whose sexual intercourse occurs only during the daytime gives birth only during the daytime; any species whose intercourse occurs only at night gives birth only at night; any species whose intercourse occurs both during the daytime and at night gives birth both during the daytime and at night.
messages.lead: § The baraita continues to discuss matters of animal procreation:

messages.text: The statement that any species whose intercourse occurs during the daytime gives birth during the daytime is referring to a chicken. The statement that any species whose intercourse occurs at night gives birth at night is referring to a bat.
messages.quote: Any species whose sexual intercourse occurs only during the daytime gives birth only during the daytime

messages.text: The statement that any species whose intercourse occurs both during the daytime and at night gives birth both during the daytime and at night is referring to a human and any creature that is similar to him.
What halakhic difference is there whether an animal gives birth during the daytime or at night?
The difference is with regard to that which Rav Mari, son of Rav Kahana, said.

If one examined a chicken’s nest on a Festival eve and did not find an egg in it, and the following day, on the Festival, he rose early, before dawn, and found an egg in it, consumption of the egg is permitted on the Festival.
messages.lead: As Rav Mari, son of Rav Kahana, said:

notes.he: קודם היום ומצא בה ביצה מותרת דלא נולדה בלילי י"ט אלא מאתמול דתרנגולת אינה יולדת בלילה כדתני לעיל. יצתה רובה מותרת דבתר יציאת רובה אזלינן:
notes.en: And the following day he rose early: before daybreak, and found an egg in it, it is permitted, since it was not laid on the night of the Festival but the day before, as a chicken does not lay at night, as was taught above. If most of it emerged, it is permitted, since we go by the emergence of the majority.

messages.text: It is not considered an egg that was laid on the Festival, which is forbidden (see Beitza 2a), as chickens do not lay eggs at night. Although he examined the nest before the Festival and failed to find an egg there, one is compelled to say that he did not examine the nest carefully.

notes.he: דלא נולד בי"ט ולא בלילה דהא אינה יולדת בלילה ודאי דאתמול היא:
notes.en: It is permitted to eat it on the Festival: since it was not laid on the Festival, nor at night, as it does not lay at night; certainly it is from yesterday.

messages.text: But he did examine the nest carefully, as the baraita states that he examined it.
messages.quote: examined a chicken’s nest on a Festival eve and did not find an egg in it

messages.text: One must say that this was a case where most of the egg emerged on the eve of the Festival and returned inside its mother before the examination. And this ruling is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yoḥanan,

notes.he: מכאן מתירין לקנות ביצים בליל שני של יו"ט של גליות חוץ משני ימים טובים של ראש השנה לפי שקדושה אחת הן:
notes.en: Say most of it emerged and returned: from here they permit buying eggs on the night of the second Festival day of the Diaspora, except for the two Festival days of Rosh HaShana, since they are one sanctity.

notes.he: והלא בדק מערב יום טוב ולא היתה שם אימור יצתה רובה ממעי תרנגולת מערב י"ט וחזרה הילכך לא מצא כי בדק וכיון שיצאה רובה וחזרה אותה ביצה שחזרה מטילה אפילו בלילה ומותר לאוכלה בי"ט. אבל לכתחלה אינה מטילה ביצה בלילה כדאמרן הילכך מותר:
notes.en: But didn’t he examine on the Festival eve? Say most of it emerged from the chicken’s belly on the Festival eve and returned; that is why he did not find it when he examined. And since most of it emerged and returned, that egg which returned is laid even at night, and it is permitted to eat it on the Festival. But in the first place a chicken does not lay an egg at night, as we said; therefore it is permitted.

messages.text: In a case where most of the egg emerged on the eve of the Festival and returned inside its mother it is permitted to eat it on the Festival, as once most of it emerged it is considered to have been laid already.
Any two animals of different species whose manner of intercourse and time of gestation are identical can have offspring together and can raise, i.e., nurse, the young of each other.

notes.he: כגון כשב ועז ששניהם פנים כנגד עורף וימי עיבורן שוה ששוהין חמשה חדשים ויולדין אם בא אחד על מין חבירו:
notes.en: Any whose intercourse and gestation are identical: such as a sheep and a goat, both of which mate face to the back of the neck, and whose days of gestation are identical, as they carry five months; they give birth if one mates with the other’s species.

notes.he: מניקין:
notes.en: And raise: nurse.

notes.dh: כל שתשמישו ועיבורו שוה כגון כל בהמה דקה טהורה שיולדת לה' חדשים היינו עיבורן שוה
notes.he: ותשמישן שוה פנים כנגד עורף. יולדים ומגדלים זה מזה כגון רחל מתיש ועז מאיל יולדין זה מזה. ומגדלין שמתקיימין וולדותיהן. וכן נמי כל בהמה גסה שעיבורה ותשמישה שוה:
notes.en: Any whose intercourse and gestation are identical: such as any small kosher livestock, which give birth after five months; that is, their gestation is identical, and their intercourse is identical, face opposite the back of the neck. They give birth to and raise one another: e.g., a ewe from a he-goat and a goat from a ram give birth from one another. And “raise”: their offspring survive. And likewise any large livestock whose gestation and intercourse are identical.

messages.text: With regard to the manner of intercourse, all species engage in intercourse with the face of the male opposite the back of the neck of the female, meaning that the male comes from behind the female, except for three species that engage in intercourse face-to-face, and they are these: Fish, and humans, and the snake.
And what is different about these three?
messages.quote: except for three species that engage in intercourse face-to-face

messages.text: They are different because the Divine Presence spoke with them. This occurred when the fish swallowed the prophet Jonah (see Jonah 2:11), when Adam and other prophets were spoken to by God, and when the snake caused Adam and Eve to sin (see Genesis 3:14).
messages.lead: When Rav Dimi came from Eretz Yisrael to Babylonia he reported that they say in the West, Eretz Yisrael, the following explanation:

notes.he: שנאמר (יונה ב׳:י״א) ויאמר ה' לדג:
notes.en: The Divine Presence [spoke] with them: as it is stated: “And the Lord spoke to the fish” (Jonah 2:11).

messages.text: A camel engages in intercourse back to back with its mate.
§ The Gemara cites a baraita that discusses the length of gestation for various animals.
A chicken hatches after twenty-one days, and corresponding to it in length of gestation with regard to trees is the almond, which ripens twenty-one days after the budding of the flower.

notes.he: לאחר שנתעברה מן התרנגול שוהה ביצתה ליגמר עד אחד ועשרים יום:
notes.en: After twenty-one days: after it has conceived from the rooster, its egg takes twenty-one days to be completed.

notes.he: קורדל"א שגדילים בו אגוזים קטנים ומשעת פרחיו עד שעת גמר פריו שנים ועשרים יום:
notes.en: Luz: (Rashi adds an Old French gloss) [a tree] on which small nuts grow; from the time it flowers until its fruit is ripe is twenty-two days [so the printed Rashi; the baraita says twenty-one]. [Rashi takes luz as a small-nut tree; the English “almond” follows the view Tosafot cite from Riva.]

notes.dh: תרנגולת כ"א יום כנגדה באילן לוז
notes.he: פי' הקונטרס קורדל"א שגדלים בו אגוזים קטנים וריב"א מפרש שקדים שקורין אמנדליי"ד דבטנים ושקדים (בראשית מג) מתרגם ירושלמי לוזים מקל שקד (ירמיהו א׳:י״א) מתרגם חוטרא דלוזא וי"מ מקל שקד אחד לכ"א אף מי"ז בתמוז לתשעה באב כן וינאץ השקד (קהלת י״ב:ה׳) מתרגם שיגדא ויגמל שקדים (במדבר י״ז:כ״ג) [מתרגם] וכפית שגדין עוד אמרינן וינאץ השקד זה לוז של שדרה ממנה עתידים מתים להחיות לעתיד לבא לוז תרגום של שקד (ויקרא רבה):
notes.en: A chicken, twenty-one days, and corresponding to it among trees, the luz: the Kuntres [Rashi] explains (Old French gloss), on which small nuts grow. Riva explains almonds, called (Old French gloss), since for “nuts and almonds” (Genesis 43:11) the Targum Yerushalmi renders luzim, and “a rod of an almond tree” (Jeremiah 1:11) is rendered “a rod of luz.” And some explain “a rod of an almond tree” as one in twenty-one, like the days from the seventeenth of Tammuz to the Ninth of Av [twenty-one days]. “And the almond tree shall blossom” (Ecclesiastes 12:5) is rendered shigda, and “it bore ripe almonds” (Numbers 17:23) is rendered “it ripened shigdin.” We also say: “And the almond tree shall blossom”: this is the luz of the spine, from which the dead are destined to be revived in the future; and luz is the Aramaic for shaked [almond] (Vayikra Rabba).

notes.he: תרנגולת יולדת לכ"א ימים מאחר שנגמר אשכול ביצים שלה וכנגדה באילן לוז משעת הנצתו עד גמר פריו כ"א יום. ואיכא דאמרי כ"א יום יושבת על ביציה. למ"ה:
notes.en: A chicken gives birth after twenty-one days, after its cluster of eggs is completed; and corresponding to it among trees is the luz, from the time it buds until its fruit is finished, twenty-one days. And some say: for twenty-one days it sits on its eggs. [The note ends with an unclear abbreviation.]

messages.text: A dog gives birth after fifty days, and corresponding to it with regard to trees is the fig. A cat gives birth after fifty-two days, and corresponding to it with regard to trees is the mulberry.

notes.he: גמרה צורת הולד:
notes.en: A dog after fifty days: [by then] the form of the fetus is completed.

notes.he: אין ראיה מכאן שמברכין עליהן בורא פרי העץ דהכי אמרינן באילן דגן דאתיא כמ"ד (ברכות דף מ.) עץ שאכל ממנו אדם הראשון חטה היתה אלמא קרי לתבואה אילן ולא מברכין בהם פרי העץ ומיהו תותים הגדלים באילן מברכין פרי העץ אבל לא אתותי שדה דאי שקלת לפירא לא הדר גווזא ומפיק ואין מברכין פרי העץ אלא כי הדר גווזא ומפיק:
notes.en: Among trees, the mulberry: there is no proof from here that one recites over them “Who creates the fruit of the tree,” for we likewise say “among trees, grain,” which follows the one who says (Berakhot 40a) that the tree from which Adam ate was wheat. Evidently grain is called a tree, and yet one does not recite “fruit of the tree” over it. However, over mulberries that grow on a tree one does recite “fruit of the tree,” but not over field mulberries [that grow on a low plant], for if you take the fruit the stem does not grow back and produce again, and one recites “fruit of the tree” only where the stem grows back and produces.

notes.he: כלב (נ"ב) [נ'] יום משעת עבורו ועד לידתו:
notes.en: A dog, fifty days [the printed text reads fifty-two, corrected to fifty]: from the time it conceives until it gives birth.

notes.he: וכנגדו באילן תאנה משעת הנצה ועד גמר פירי:
notes.en: And corresponding to it among trees is the fig: from the time of budding until the fruit is finished.

messages.text: A pig gives birth after sixty days, and corresponding to it with regard to trees is the apple. A fox and all types of creeping animals give birth after six months, and corresponding to them with regard to trees, i.e., plants, is grain.

notes.he: כמאן דאמר (ברכות דף מ.) עץ שאכל אדם הראשון חטה היתה קרי לתבואה אילן:
notes.en: And corresponding to them among trees is grain: according to the one who says (Berakhot 40a) that the tree from which Adam ate was wheat, grain is called a tree.

notes.he: דתבואה איקרו אילן כמאן דאמר אילן שאכל אדה"ר ממנו חטין הוו. ששה חדשים משעת זריעה עד שעושין שיבולת:
notes.en: And corresponding to them among trees is grain: for grain is called a tree, according to the one who says the tree from which Adam ate was wheat. Six months from the time of sowing until they form ears.

messages.text: Small kosher livestock, such as sheep or goats, give birth after five months, and corresponding to them with regard to trees is the grapevine. Large non-kosher livestock, such as camels or donkeys, give birth after twelve months, and corresponding to them with regard to trees is the date palm.

notes.he: גדילין בו תמרים:
notes.en: Date palm: on which dates grow.

messages.text: Large kosher livestock, such as cows, give birth after nine months, and corresponding to them with regard to trees is the olive.

The wolf, and the lion, and the bear, and the leopard, and the bardelas, and the elephant, and the monkey, and the long-tailed ape give birth after three years, and corresponding to them with regard to trees is the white fig.

notes.he: אפא:
notes.en: Bardelas: [the animal called] afa.

notes.he: שיניי"א בלע"ז:
notes.en: Monkey: (Rashi adds an Old French gloss.)

notes.he: כעין קוף הוא ויש לה זנב ובלשון אשכנז מרקצ"א:
notes.en: Kipof [the long-tailed ape]: it is like a monkey and has a tail. (Rashi adds a German gloss.)

notes.he: פ"ה אפא ופ"ק דסנהדרין (דף טו:) פ"ה פוטו"ש וסוף פ"ק דב"ק (דף טז.) [אמרינן] ברדלס [זו] אפא ואמרינן צבוע זה אפא וגיא הצבועים (שמואל א יג) מתרגם מישר אפעיא מיהו ברדלס דהכא משמעו דהוא כעין פוטו"ש ויולד לשלש שנים מדשינה אפעה לשבעים שנה וב' מיני ברדלס הן:
notes.en: Bardelas: Rashi explains afa; in the first chapter of Sanhedrin (15b) Rashi explains (Old French gloss); and at the end of the first chapter of Bava Kamma (16a) we say that the bardelas is the afa, and we say that the tzavua [hyena] is the afa, and “the valley of Tzevo’im” (I Samuel 13:18) is rendered “the plain of Afaya.” But the bardelas here seems to be like the (Old French gloss), and it gives birth after three years, since [the baraita] lists the viper [efe] separately, at seventy years. There are two kinds of bardelas.

notes.he: מין חיה הוא מדחשיב להו בהדי פיל ואמר פ' הרואה (ברכות דף נז:) כל מיני חיות יפין לחלום חוץ מן הפיל והקיפוף ופ' המפלת (נדה דף כג.) אמרינן ל"א ר"מ אומר הואיל ועיניהם הולכים לפניהם כשל אדם והוא כוס וינשוף (ויקרא יא) מתרגם קריא וקפופא ויש קפוף אחר מין עוף פרק אלו טריפות (חולין דף סג.) אמר תנשמת באות שבעופות ואמר באות שבעופות קפוף ויש גרס קיפוד בדל"ת ע"ד וירשוה קאת וקיפוד (ישעיהו לד) ואי גרס קיפוף ותרי גווני קיפוף יש בעופות א"כ כי מפרש באות שבעופות קפוף והיכי ידענא בהו אי איירי בינשוף או בתנשמת:
notes.en: The kof and the kipof: [the kipof] is a kind of wild animal, since they are counted together with the elephant. In chapter HaRo’eh (Berakhot 57b) it says that all kinds of animals are good in a dream except for the elephant and the kipof. In chapter HaMappelet (Nidda 23a) we say: “Some say Rabbi Meir says: since their eyes are set in front like those of a person.” And “the kos and the yanshuf” (Leviticus 11:17) are rendered kaya and kafofa. There is also another kipof, a kind of bird: in chapter Elu Tereifot (Ḥullin 63a) it says the tinshemet is the ba’ot among birds, and it says the ba’ot among birds is the kipof. Some read kipod, with a dalet, following “the ka’at and the kipod shall possess it” (Isaiah 34:11). But if one reads kipof, and there are two kinds of kipof among birds, then when it explains that the ba’ot among birds is the kipof, how would we know whether it speaks of the yanshuf or of the tinshemet?

notes.he: תאנים חיורתא. וימי עיבורו של חרוב הנצתו שלשה שנים אחרונים של ע' שנים:
notes.en: Shuaḥ [benot shuaḥ, rendered “white fig” in the English]: white figs. And the gestation of the carob is its budding, the last three years of the seventy years.

messages.text: A viper gives birth after seventy years, and corresponding to it with regard to trees is the carob. In the case of this carob, the period from the time of its planting until the time of the ripening of its fruit is seventy years, and the length of its gestation is three years.

notes.he: מתעבר אחר שבעים שנה שנולד:
notes.en: A viper: it conceives seventy years after it was born.

notes.he: משעת הפרח עד שעת גמר פירות:
notes.en: And the days of its gestation: from the time of the flowering until the time the fruit is completed.

messages.text: A snake is born after seven years, and for that wicked animal we have not found a counterpart among trees. And some say that mukhsasim are the equivalent, as they ripen after seven years.

notes.he: מין בנות שוח ולא בנות שוח ממש:
notes.en: Mukhsasim: a kind of benot shuaḥ [a variety of fig], but not benot shuaḥ proper.

notes.he: על משנה דשביעית שלהן בשניה (שביעית פ"ה מ"א) פי' בירושלמי בכל שנה חונטין בה פירות ופירות שחונטין בשנה אחת אין נגמרין עד שלש שנים ולא כפי' ר"ח שפירש גבי ל' אילנות לא מפקין בכל שתא אלא עשרים מנייהו כגון בנות שוח לג' שנים ופ"ק דע"ז (דף יד.) גרס מוכססים בנות שוח מין אחד וכן שמו וקשה במסכת דמאי (פ"א מ"א) תנן הקלין שבדמאי לא נחשדו עמי הארץ עליהן משמע דלאו פירי חשוב נינהו ופ"ק דמסכת ע"ז (דף יד.) מפרש תאיני חיורתא ופרק ג' דנדרים (דף כז.) בנות שבע ותאנים לבנים שני מינין דאמר אילו הייתי יודע שבנות שבע בתוך כלכלה הייתי אומר תאנים לבנות ושחורות אסורות בנות שבע מותרות ונראה בנות שוח ושבע מיני תאנים הן אלא שבנות שוח רעות כדמשמע במתני' דהקלין שבדמאי ובההיא דשביעית כסבור שאין שביעית נוהג בהן ובנות שבע יפות כדמשמע בשביעית (פ"ה) ובנדרים (דף כז.) ומסתמא אדם מן היפות אכל ונקראו שבע מן שבעת ימי אבלות ושוח שגרמו שוחה ותולין הקלקלה במקולקל:
notes.en: In brief: Benot shuaḥ: on the mishna in Shevi’it (5:1) that their Sabbatical year falls in the second year, the Yerushalmi explains that they set fruit every year, and fruit set in one year is not finished until three years. This is not like Rabbeinu Ḥananel, who explained, on the thirty trees of which only twenty yield each year, that benot shuaḥ yield every three years. In Avoda Zara (14a) the reading is “mukhsasim, benot shuaḥ” as one kind, and that is its name. A difficulty: the mishna in Demai (1:1) lists them among the lenient items that the unlearned were not suspected of, implying they are not a valued fruit; Avoda Zara (14a) explains them as white figs; and Nedarim (27a) treats benot sheva and white figs as two kinds (“had I known benot sheva were in the basket…”). Tosafot conclude that benot shuaḥ and benot sheva are both kinds of fig: benot shuaḥ are the poor ones, as the Demai and Shevi’it mishnayot imply, and benot sheva the good ones, as Shevi’it (5) and Nedarim (27a) imply. Presumably Adam ate of the good ones; they are called sheva after the seven days of mourning, and shuaḥ because they caused him to be bowed down, and the damage is ascribed to the poor kind. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

notes.he: תאנים רעות:
notes.en: Mukhsasin: poor figs.

messages.caption: The baraita’s gestation periods, each matched with a tree, in the baraita’s order.

messages.text: From where is this matter, that the gestation period of a snake is seven years, derived?
messages.quote: A snake is born after seven years

messages.alt: and some determined it to be in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Ḥananya
messages.text: It is derived from that which is stated with regard to the punishment of the snake for causing Adam and Eve to sin: “Cursed are you from among all animals, and from among all beasts of the field” (Genesis 3:14), in that your gestation period should be longer than all of them.

verse.he: וַיֹּאמֶר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהִים ׀ אֶל־הַנָּחָשׁ כִּי עָשִׂיתָ זֹּאת אָרוּר אַתָּה מִכׇּל־הַבְּהֵמָה וּמִכֹּל חַיַּת הַשָּׂדֶה עַל־גְּחֹנְךָ תֵלֵךְ וְעָפָר תֹּאכַל כׇּל־יְמֵי חַיֶּיךָ׃
verse.en:
Then the ETERNAL God said to the serpent,
“Because you did this,
More cursed shall you be
Than all cattle
And all the wild beasts:
On your belly shall you crawl
And dirt shall you eat
All the days of your life.

messages.text: Now, why does the verse mention the beasts of the field, i.e., undomesticated animals? If the snake was cursed more than the domesticated animals, then all the more so is it not clear that it was cursed more than the undomesticated animals? The shortest gestation period of domesticated animals, which is five months for a goat, is longer than the shortest gestation period among undomesticated animals, which is fifty-two days for a cat.

notes.he: דנחש עיבורו שבע שנים:
notes.en: From where are these matters derived: that the snake’s gestation is seven years.

notes.dh: אם מבהמה נתקלל מחיה לא כ"ש
notes.he: שפחותה יותר מן חיה שהרי עז ה' חדשים וחתול נ"ב [יום] והא ל"ל דהא מכל חיה היינו ארי או אפעה דא"כ ליכתוב מכל החיה ולא ליבעי בהמה:
notes.en: If it was cursed more than the domesticated animals, is it not all the more so more than the wild animals: for [domesticated animals] are lower than wild animals, since a goat takes five months and a cat fifty-two [days]. And one cannot say that “from all the beasts” means the lion or the viper, for if so, let it write “from all the beasts” and it would not need “animals.”

notes.he: מבהמה נתקלל דבהמה דקה מאחרת יותר לילד מחיה דקה קטנה לא כל שכן דבהמה דקה לה' חדשים וחיה דקה לנ"ב יום כגון חתול וכלב:
notes.en: If it was cursed more than the domesticated animals: for small domesticated animals are later to give birth than small, little wild animals, is it not all the more so? For small domesticated animals give birth at five months, and a small wild animal at fifty-two days, such as a cat and a dog.

messages.text: Rather, the verse mentions the beasts of the field to tell you: Just as the domesticated animals were cursed more than the undomesticated animals by a proportion of one to seven;

notes.dh: אלא להכי כתב תרוייהו לומר לך כו'
notes.he: והכי משמע ארור הוא מכל הבהמה כמה שהיא ארורה יותר מן החיה כשם שהבהמה נתקללה מן החיה על אחת ז' ומאי ניהו חמור מחתול שבשנה יש ז' פעמים נ"ב כך נתקלל הוא מן הבהמה כגון מבהמה גסה טמאה אחד לשבע דבהמה טמאה גסה י"ב חדש וחשוב ז' פעמים י"ב חדש היינו אחד לשבע הן שבע שנים:
notes.en: Rather, it wrote both of them to tell you, etc.: and this is the meaning: it is cursed from all the domesticated animals as much as [the domesticated animal] is cursed more than the wild animal. Just as the domesticated animal was cursed more than the wild animal one to seven, and what is that? A donkey compared to a cat, for a year holds seven times fifty-two [days], so it was cursed more than the domesticated animal, namely large non-kosher livestock, one to seven: large non-kosher livestock carries twelve months, and seven times twelve months, which is one to seven, makes seven years.

messages.text: And with regard to what case is that? It is with regard to a donkey, whose gestation period as mentioned is twelve months, compared to a cat, whose gestation period is fifty-two days. Seven times longer than fifty-two days is 364 days, which means that the gestation period of the donkey, which is one year, is almost exactly seven times longer than that of the cat.

notes.he: דחתול לנ"ב יום ותימה למ"ד כלב מין חיה כדאיתא במסכת ביצה (דף כה:) שלשה עזין הן כלב [בחיות] לנקוט חמור מכלב דמקולקל טפי שהכלב לנ' יום י"ל מנין זה מכוון טפי דהוי שנים:
notes.en: And what is that? A donkey compared to a cat: since a cat is fifty-two days. And it is puzzling, according to the one who says that a dog is a kind of wild animal, as in tractate Beitza (25b), “three are bold: the dog among wild animals”: let it take a donkey compared to a dog, which is more defective, since the dog is fifty days. One can say: this number is more exact, since it comes to a year.

notes.he: אלא למה נאמרו מכל חית אלא לומר לך כשם שהבהמה נתקללה מחיה אחד לשבע ומאי ניהו חמור מחתול דחתול לנ"ב יום ובהמה גסה טמאה לי"ב חדש דהיינו שס"ה ימים וש"נ ימים היינו ז' פעמים נ' נשתיירו ט"ו היינו ז"פ נ"ב לחתול כך הוא נתקלל מבהמה טמאה אחד לשבע דהוה ליה שב שני:
notes.en: Rather, why was “from all the beasts” stated? To tell you: just as the domesticated animals were cursed more than the wild animals one to seven, and what is that? A donkey compared to a cat, for a cat is fifty-two days and large non-kosher livestock twelve months, which is 365 days; 350 days is seven times fifty, and the fifteen that remain make it seven times fifty-two for the cat. So too it was cursed more than the non-kosher animal, one to seven, which comes to seven years.

messages.text: So too, the snake was cursed more than domesticated animals, i.e., the donkey, in a proportion of one to seven, which is a total of seven years.

Say that the verse can be interpreted as follows: Just as the undomesticated animals were cursed more than the domesticated animals by a measure of one year to three years; and in what case is that? It is in the case of a lion, whose gestation period is three years, compared to a donkey, whose gestation period is one year.
messages.quote: Cursed are you from among all animals, and from among all beasts of the field

notes.he: ואימא כשם שנתקללה חיה מבהמה אחד לשלש ומאי ניהו ארי מחמור כו':
notes.en: And say: just as the wild animals were cursed more than the domesticated animals one to three, and what is that? A lion compared to a donkey, etc.

messages.text: So too, the snake was cursed more than the undomesticated animals, i.e., the lion, by a proportion of one year to three years, which is nine years.
8b

Is it written: Cursed are you from among all beasts, and from among all animals? No, it is written: “From among all animals, and from among all beasts,” meaning that it is cursed from among the domesticated animals, which were cursed from among the undomesticated animals.

notes.dh: מי כתיב מכל החיה ומכל הבהמה
notes.he: דנידרוש מכל החיה שנתקללה יותר מבהמה:
notes.en: Is it written “from all the beasts and from all the animals,” that we should expound: from all the beasts, which were cursed more than the domesticated animals?

notes.he: משמע מבהמה המקוללת יותר כך נתקלל ואין לך מקוללת בבהמה גסה יותר מחמור]:
notes.en: [“From all the animals” is written: implying that it was cursed as much as the most cursed of the domesticated animals; and among large livestock you have none more cursed than the donkey.]

messages.text: Why must it mean that the snake was cursed more than the donkey in the same proportion that the donkey was cursed more than the cat? But say instead that just as the domesticated animals were cursed more than the undomesticated animals by a measure of one to three; and in what case is that? It is in the case of a goat, whose gestation period is five months, compared to a cat, whose gestation period is fifty-two days.

notes.dh: כך נתקלל הוא מבהמה אחד לשלש
notes.he: כגון בהמה דקה טהורה דעיבורה לה' חדשים ובג' זימני (תלתא) הוי ט"ו:
notes.en: So too it was cursed more than the domesticated animals one to three: such as small kosher livestock, whose gestation is five months, and three times that is fifteen.

notes.dh: אחד לשלש ומאי נינהו עז מחתול
notes.he: הכא ניחא טפי למנקט עז מכלב למ"ד (כלאים פ"ח מ"ו) מין חיה לפי שהחשבון שלהן מכוון טפי אחד לשלש אלא ניחא ליה למיפרך ככולי עלמא:
notes.en: One to three; and what is that? A goat compared to a cat: here it would have been better to take a goat compared to a dog, according to the one who says (Kilayim 8:6) [that the dog] is a kind of wild animal, since their numbers fit one to three more exactly. But it preferred to challenge according to everyone.

notes.dh: ואימא כשם שנתקללה בהמה מחיה אחד לשלש ומאי ניהו עז מחתול
notes.he: דחתול (לנ') [לנ"ב] יום ועז לה' חדשים דהיינו ג' פעמים נ"ב:
notes.en: And say: just as the domesticated animals were cursed more than the wild animals one to three, and what is that? A goat compared to a cat: for a cat is fifty-two days and a goat five months, which is three times fifty-two.

messages.text: So too, the snake was cursed more than the domesticated animals, i.e., the goat, by a proportion of one to three, which is fifteen months.
If you wish, say that it is written: “Cursed are you from among all animals,” including the most accursed of them, i.e., the donkey.

notes.he: דמשמע מכל הבהמה המקוללת יותר:
notes.en: If you wish, say “from all the animals”: which implies, from all the animals, the most cursed one.

notes.he: מבהמה שמקוללת יותר מחיה דהיינו אחד לשבע כדאמרן:
notes.en: If you wish, say: “from all the animals” is written: from the domesticated animal that is cursed more than the wild animal, that is, one to seven, as we said.

messages.text: If you wish, say instead that since it is a curse that the snake received here, the verse imposes upon it the most extreme curse that can be derived from the text.

notes.he: לשם קללה נאמר הלכך קללה חמורה שתוכל לדרוש מן הפסוק שדי עילויה. והכי נמי איכא לאקשויי ואימא כשם שנתקללה בהמה מחיה אחד לשנים ומאי ניהו חמור משועל כך נתקלל הוא מחמור אחד לשנים דהוו להו ב' שנים אלא איכא לתרוצי קללה שדי עילויה ועוד מכל הבהמה ומכל החיה כתיב דמשמע דמשום בהמה שיתירה קללתה על שום חיה ומצינו חמור מקולל מחתול אחד לשבע:
notes.en: And if you wish, say: it was stated as a curse; therefore impose upon it the severest curse you can expound from the verse. One could similarly challenge: say, just as the domesticated animals were cursed more than the wild animals one to two, and what is that? A donkey compared to a fox, so it was cursed more than the donkey one to two, which comes to two years. But one can answer: impose the curse upon it. Moreover, “from all the animals and from all the beasts” is written, which implies [it is measured] by the domesticated animal whose curse exceeds that of the wild animal, and we found the donkey cursed more than the cat, one to seven.

notes.he: איבעית תימא קללה הוא כיון דמתקלל רמינן ליה בתר בהמה דנתקללה טפי מחיה:
notes.en: If you wish, say: it is a curse; since it is being cursed, we place it after the domesticated animal that was cursed most relative to the wild animal.

notes.he: קללה טפי:
notes.en: Impose upon it: more of a curse.

messages.caption: Three ways to read the snake’s curse as a ratio, and why the Gemara keeps seven years.

messages.text: In the case of a snake, after how long a period of gestation does it give birth?
messages.lead: § With regard to the gestation time of a snake, the Gemara relates that the Roman emperor said to Rabbi Yehoshua ben Ḥananya:

notes.he: כמה שוהה עיבורו במעיו:
notes.en: After how long does it conceive and give birth: how long its gestation stays in its belly.

messages.text: @The Emperor After seven years.
But the elders, i.e., the sages, of the school of Athens bred snakes and they gave birth after three years.

notes.he: מקום:
notes.en: Of Atuna: a place.

notes.he: נחש זכר על הנקבה ושמום במשמר ואוליד לתלת שני:
notes.en: They mated them: a male snake on the female, and they placed them under guard, and it gave birth after three years.

messages.text: Those snakes were already pregnant from beforehand for four years.
messages.quote: they gave birth after three years

notes.he: דאוליד לתלת שני ודאי מעברא הוו מעיקרא ארבע שני קודם שהרביעום:
notes.en: Those: that gave birth after three years were certainly pregnant at the outset, four years before they mated them.

messages.text: But they engaged in intercourse, and animals do so only in order to give birth, not when they are already pregnant.

notes.he: ואי הוו מעברי לא הוו משמשי שדרך חיה ובהמה מאחר שנתעברה אינה מקבלת זכר:
notes.en: But they engaged in intercourse: and had they been pregnant they would not have engaged in intercourse, for the way of a wild or domesticated animal is that once it has conceived it does not accept a male.

notes.he: כשהרביעום ואי הוה הנקבה מעוברת וודאי לא הוה מקבלה זכר שכן דרך כל הבהמות שלאחר שמתעברות אינן מקבלות זכר:
notes.en: But they engaged in intercourse: when they mated them; and had the female been pregnant, it certainly would not have accepted a male, for such is the way of all animals: after they conceive they do not accept a male.

messages.text: Snakes also engage in intercourse like people, i.e., they do not do so solely for reproduction.

notes.he: הנחשים משמשי כאדם פנים נגד פנים וכיון דמשמשי כאדם משמשי נמי לבתר דמתעברי כאדם:
notes.en: They too: the snakes engage in intercourse like a person, face to face; and since they engage like a person, they also engage after they have conceived, like a person.

messages.text: But how can you disagree with the sages of Athens? Aren’t they wise?

notes.he: הנהו סבי וירדו לסוף המעשה:
notes.en: But they are wise: those elders, and they get to the bottom of a matter.

notes.he: סבי דבי אתונא בשאר מילי וחכימי נמי בהאי דאמרי לתלת שני:
notes.en: But they are wise: the elders of the school of Atuna, in other matters, and they are wise in this too, in saying three years.

messages.text: We are wiser than they.

notes.he: ואנן ידעינן לכל מילתא שפיר מנייהו:
notes.en: We are wiser than they: we know every matter better than they do.

messages.text: If you are wiser than they, then go defeat them in debate and bring them to me.

notes.he: נצחם:
notes.en: Go defeat them: overcome them.

notes.he: כלומר התערב עמהם בדברי חכמה ועשה תנאי עמהם אם תנצחם שילכו עמך ואיתיניהו לי:
notes.en: Go defeat them: that is, engage them in matters of wisdom and make a condition with them that if you defeat them they will go with you; and bring them to me.

messages.text: @The Emperor How many are there?
Sixty men.

notes.he: א"ל כמה הוו הנהו סבי א"ל שיתין:
notes.en: He said to him: How many are those elders? He said to him: Sixty.

messages.text: @The Emperor Construct a ship that has sixty rooms for me, and each room should have sixty mattresses [bistarkei] in it.

notes.he: כסאות:
notes.en: Bistarkei: seats. [The English renders “mattresses.”]

notes.he: כסאות מקושטין הרבה:
notes.en: Sixty bistarkei: many ornamented seats.

messages.text: The emperor constructed it for him. Rabbi Yehoshua then set out on the ship for Athens. When he arrived there, he entered a butcher shop and found a certain man, the butcher, flaying an animal.

notes.he: לכרך שלהם:
notes.en: When he arrived there: at their city.

notes.he: מחתך בהמה:
notes.en: Doing an animal: cutting up an animal.

notes.he: לאתריהו על לבי טבחא כו':
notes.en: When he arrived there: at their place, at a butcher shop, etc.

messages.text: @The Butcher Is your head for sale?
@Rabbi Yehoshua Yes it is.
For how much is it being sold?
For half a dinar.
Rabbi Yehoshua gave him the money.
Did I say to you that I wanted the head of the animal? I was referring to your head, and you must now keep your word and give me your head.
messages.lead: After Rabbi Yehoshua paid the butcher, he said to him:

notes.he: בתמיה:
notes.en: And did I say to you the head of the animal? Said as a question [I did not].

messages.text: If you wish for me to let you be, go and show me the entrance to the school of the sages of Athens.

notes.he: צעוד ולך לפני:
notes.en: Sagi: step forward and go before me.

messages.text: @Rabbi Yehoshua I am afraid, as they kill anyone who shows its location to another.
@The Butcher Carry a bundle of reeds, and when you arrive there, stand it up like one who is resting, to mark the location.

notes.he: טול חבילה של קנים וכי מטית התם נגד הפתח זקוף החבילה לארץ:
notes.en: Carry a bundle of reeds: take a bundle of reeds, and when you get there, opposite the entrance, stand the bundle up on the ground.

notes.he: כאדם העומד לפוש:
notes.en: Like one who is resting: like a person who stops to rest.

notes.he: כנגד פיתחיהן כמאן דקא מתפח ויראה לבני אדם כמו שתעשה כדי לנוח ממשואך ולא ירגישו בך ובכך אדע פיתחן:
notes.en: Stand it up: opposite their entrance, like one who is resting; it will look to people as though you are doing this to rest from your load, and they will not notice you, and that way I will know their entrance.

messages.text: The butcher did this, and Rabbi Yehoshua successfully found the entrance.

Rabbi Yehoshua found guards stationed on the inside and guards stationed on the outside to ensure that no one could enter or exit. They also spread sand on the ground in the entranceway so that they could detect if anyone entered or left.

notes.he: ר' יהושע:
notes.en: He went: Rabbi Yehoshua.

notes.he: אורבים:
notes.en: He found guards: lurkers.

notes.he: שלא יצא אחד מן הזקנים לחוץ:
notes.en: Outside: so that none of the elders would go out.

notes.he: שהיו סובין מושלכין שם מבפנים הפתח ומבחוץ. ואית דאמרי דרבוני שומרים מבראי ומגואי:
notes.en: He found bran inside: bran was scattered there, inside the entrance and outside. And some say darbonei are guards, outside and inside.

messages.text: If they saw footsteps that were entering they would kill the outer guards for allowing people to enter, and if they saw footsteps that were exiting they would kill the inner guards for allowing people to leave.

notes.he: שלא יניחו אדם ליכנס וכי חזו הנך סבי כרעא דעיילא קטלי להו [לבראי] שהיתה אסקופת החדר עבה ושופכין סובין או עפר עליה וניכרות בה פסיעות האדם וכי חזו כרעא דעיילא קטלי לשומרי [בראי] כי הניחו לבא וכי חזו כרעא דנפקא קטלי להו [לגוואי] שהניחוהו לצאת והשומרים לא היו הורגים שום אדם אא"כ נכנס כולו לפנים על כרחן או אחד יוצא כולו לחוץ:
notes.en: Inside: so that they would not let anyone enter. And when those elders saw an entering footprint they killed [the outer guards]. For the threshold of the room was thick, and they would pour bran or dust on it, and a person’s steps showed in it. When they saw an entering footprint they killed the [outer] guards, for letting him come in; and when they saw an exiting footprint they killed the [inner] ones, for letting him go out. And the guards would not kill anyone, unless one forced his way entirely inside or one went entirely outside.

notes.he: רושם כרעא דעיילא קטלי לשומרים דאבראי דשבקי גברא למיעל. ואי חזו רושם כרעא דנפקא קטלי לשומרים דגואי:
notes.en: For if they saw: the mark of an entering foot, they would kill the outer guards, who let a man in; and if they saw the mark of an exiting foot, they would kill the inner guards.

messages.text: Rabbi Yehoshua reversed his sandal so it was facing away from the entrance, walked on the sand, and snuck away, thereby creating the appearance of someone who had left the building. When the authorities saw the footsteps, they killed the inner guards.

notes.he: רבי יהושע לסנדליה ועמד על האיסקופה ונראית פסיעה אחת נכנסת ופסיעה אחת יוצאה ודחפוהו השומרים ויצא וכשבאו הזקנים ראו כן ודימו ששני בני אדם הן אחד נכנס ואחד יוצא וקטלינהו לכולהו שומרים ואח"כ נכנס רבי יהושע:
notes.en: He reversed: Rabbi Yehoshua reversed his sandal and stood on the threshold, and there appeared one step entering and one step exiting. The guards pushed him and he went out. When the elders came and saw this, they imagined that there were two people, one entering and one leaving, and they killed all the guards. Afterward Rabbi Yehoshua went in.

messages.text: Rabbi Yehoshua then returned, reversed his sandal, and made footsteps in the sand indicating that someone had entered the building. They then killed all the guards, including the outer ones, and Rabbi Yehoshua succeeded in entering the building.

notes.he: אזל ר' יהושע עיין בשעה שישנו השומרים ואפכיה לסנדל חדא העקב לפניו והאחד הניח כמו שהוא ונראה האחד כנכנס והאחד כיוצא. (ונכנס) וכיון שראו שהפסיעות כך קטלינהו לכולהו שומרים:
notes.en: Rabbi Yehoshua went and watched for the time when the guards slept, and reversed one sandal, the heel in front, and left the other as it was; and one appeared to be entering and the other leaving. Once they saw the steps like this, they killed all the guards.

messages.text: Rabbi Yehoshua found the younger sages sitting in the upper, more prominent section, and the elder ones in the lower section.

notes.he: בעלייה. ולהרע נתכוונו שהנותן שלום לעליונים תחלה הורגים אותו התחתונים ואומרים אנו הזקנים ולנו היה לך ליתן שלום תחילה והנותן שלום לזקנים הורגין אותו הבחורים ואומרים הלא אנו חשובים מהם שאנחנו למעלה והם למטה:
notes.en: Youngsters above: in the upper story. They intended harm: one who greets the upper ones first, the lower ones kill him, saying, “We are the elders, and you should have greeted us first”; and one who greets the elders, the young men kill him, saying, “Are we not more important than they, for we are above and they are below?”

notes.he: אשכח ינוקי מלעיל וסבי מלתחת כדי להעליל על האדם אם יקדים שלום לאלו או לאלו:
notes.en: He found the youngsters above and the elders below: in order to bring a charge against a person whether he greets these first or those.

messages.text: I must first greet the younger sages, as they are sitting in the upper section, prior to the elder sages; but if I greet these younger sages first, those elder sages will kill me, as they maintain: We are better, because we are older and they are children.
Greetings to you.
messages.lead: Rabbi Yehoshua said, without directly addressing either group:

messages.text: What are you doing here?

notes.he: מאי בעית הכא:
notes.en: What is your business: what do you want here?

messages.text: I am a Sage of the Jews, and I desire to learn wisdom from you.
If so, we will ask you questions and see if you are worthy of this privilege.

notes.he: דחכימא את ניבעי אנן מינך:
notes.en: If so: that you are wise, let us ask you.

messages.text: Very well. If you win, you may do to me anything you wish, and if I defeat you, then eat with me on my ship.

notes.he: אם תנצחוני:
notes.en: If you defeat me: if you overcome me.

messages.text: @Rabbi Yehoshua In the case of a certain man who goes and asks to marry a woman and her family does not give her to him, why would he see fit to go to a family that is greater than the first?

notes.he: שמיוחסת מן הראשונה ושואל אותה הרי יש לו ללמד הואיל ולא נתנו לו את הראשונה כל שכן זו:
notes.en: Greater than it: of better lineage than the first, and he asks for her. Surely he should learn: since they did not give him the first, all the more so this one.

messages.text: In this case too, where he goes to a more distinguished family than the first, perhaps he will find the girl destined for him.
messages.lead: Rabbi Yehoshua took a peg and stuck it into the lower part of the wall, but it did not go in. He then stuck it into the upper portion of the wall where there was a hole, and it went in. He said to them:
messages.quote: why would he see fit to go to a family that is greater than the first

notes.he: קביליי"א:
notes.en: Sikhta: a peg. (Rashi adds an Old French gloss.)

notes.he: דצה השפיל ידו ונעצה בכותל במקום שאין חור ולא על דלי דצה הגביה [ידו] ודצה במקום שיש חור ועל:
notes.en: He stuck it low: he lowered his hand and stuck it into the wall at a place where there was no hole, and it did not go in; [he stuck it] high: he raised [his hand] and stuck it where there was a hole, and it went in.

notes.he: יתד:
notes.en: Sikhta: a peg.

notes.he: נעצה בכותל לתתאי במקום (שלא) כנגד אבן שלא היה נקב לא עאל. דצה לעילאי במקום בין אבן לאבן שהיה נקב ועאל הכי נמי פעמים כשישאל מיוחסת מן הראשונה שמא היא תהיה מזלו:
notes.en: He stuck it into the wall low, in a place opposite a stone where there was no hole: it did not go in. He stuck it high, in a place between stone and stone where there was a hole, and it went in. So too, sometimes, when one asks for a woman of better lineage than the first, perhaps she will be his destined match.

messages.text: In the case of a man who lends money to an individual and the borrower does not repay the loan, and the lender repossesses the borrower’s property as payment instead, why would he see fit to lend to others again?

notes.he: שהלוה מעות לחבירו ולא נפרע ממנו אלא בקושי שטרף לקוחות:
notes.en: A man who lends and repossesses: who lent money to his fellow and was repaid only with difficulty, in that he seized property from buyers.

notes.he: לאחריני ולא נתייסר מן הראשון:
notes.en: Why would he see fit to lend again: to others, and not take a lesson from the first?

messages.text: This is what people do: If a man goes to the pond, initially cuts a bundle of reeds, but finds that he cannot lift it, he does not stop cutting wood. Instead, he cuts more wood and places it upon the first, until a person happens to pass by and helps him raise it upon his shoulders, so that he can carry it home.
messages.quote: why would he see fit to lend to others again?

notes.he: ליער:
notes.en: To the agma: to the forest.

notes.he: חתך חבילה ראשונה ולא מצי ביה להרימו על שכמו:
notes.en: He cut a first bundle: he cut a first bundle and could not lift it onto his shoulder.

messages.text: So too, a person continues to lend based on the assumption that he will eventually find an appropriate borrower.

notes.he: הואיל וצריך סיוע אחרים עד דמיתרמי' איניש ומדלו ליה. והאי נמי הואיל והפסיד באמנה ראשונה חוזר ומאמין לאחרים עד שמזדווג לו לאדם נאמן ומשתכר בו:
notes.en: He cuts more and places it upon it: since he needs the help of others anyway, until someone happens by and lifts it for him. So too this one: since he lost on his first trust, he goes on trusting others until he is matched with a trustworthy person and profits by him.

notes.he: וכשבא לגבותן טרף להו בצער ע"י ב"ד. מאי חזי דהדר יזיף לאיניש אחרינא. אמר להו גברא אזיל לאגמא קטיל טונא קמא דקני והוה כל כך נפיש דלא מצי ביה למיטעניה וקא מוסיף וקטל ומנח עילויה ההוא טונא אלא להכי מוסיף וקטיל ומנח עליה דסבר עד דמיתרמי לי איניש דמסייעי לי דאידלי על כתפאי. אף האי הדר ויזיף דסבר הא בעל חוב בתרא הוא נוח מן הראשון:
notes.en: A man who lends money to someone and repossesses: when he comes to collect it, he seizes it with distress, through the court. Why would he see fit to lend again to another person? He said to them: A man goes to the marsh and cuts a first bundle of reeds, and it was so big that he cannot load it; and he goes on cutting and places more on that bundle. He adds, cuts and places it on top only because he thinks: until someone happens by who will help me lift it onto my shoulders. So too this one lends again, since he thinks: this last debtor will be easier than the first.

messages.text: Say to us a matter of nonsense.

notes.he: דברי רוח. ל"א מילי דכזיב דברי כזב:
notes.en: Matters of kedi: words of wind. Another version: matters of kazav, words of falsehood.

notes.he: משלים של כזב:
notes.en: Matters of nonsense: parables of falsehood.

messages.text: There was a certain mule that gave birth, and a note was hanging on the newborn mule’s neck and on it was written that it is owed 100,000 dinars by its father’s household.

notes.he: פרידה:
notes.en: Kudanita: a female mule.

notes.he: שטר בצוואר הוולד:
notes.en: And a note was hanging: a document on the newborn’s neck.

messages.text: But can a mule give birth?
messages.quote: a certain mule that gave birth

messages.text: This is why it is a matter of nonsense, as it is impossible for a mule to give birth.

notes.he: אלו הן דברי רוח:
notes.en: These are matters of kedi: these are words of wind.

messages.text: When salt is spoiling, with what does one salt it to preserve it?
With the placenta of a mule.

notes.he: שיליא:
notes.en: Silita: the placenta.

messages.text: But is there a placenta of a mule?
And does salt spoil?
Build us a house in the air of the world.
Bring up to me bricks and mortar and I will build you a house here.
messages.lead: Rabbi Yehoshua uttered a Name of God and hovered between the sky and the earth. He said to them:

notes.dh: אמר שם ותלא נפשיה בין רקיעא לארעא
notes.he: אמר להו אסיקו לי ליבני וטונא באוירא ולא יכלי:
notes.en: He uttered a Name and suspended himself between sky and earth. He said to them: Bring up bricks and mortar to me in the air; and they could not.

messages.text: Where is the center of the world?
Here.
messages.lead: Rabbi Yehoshua raised his finger and said to them:

messages.text: And who says that you are correct?
Bring ropes and measure.
We have a pit in the field; bring it to the city.
Braid ropes made of bran for me and I will bring it to the city with them.

notes.he: עשו לי חבלים מסובין ואם אינכם עושין שאילתי אף אני לא אעשה שאילתכם:
notes.en: Of bran: make me ropes of bran; and if you do not do what I ask, I too will not do what you ask.

messages.text: We have a mill that broke; sew it back together.

notes.he: תפור אותה:
notes.en: Sew it: sew it.

messages.text: Pull out threads from the mill for me and I will sew them together.

notes.he: הוציאו לי ממנה חוטין כדרך נשים שמוציאין חוטין מן הבגד ותופרין אותו בהן:
notes.en: Pull out threads from it for me: draw threads out of it for me, the way women draw threads out of a garment and sew it with them.

notes.he: בלע"ז פירנ"ש:
notes.en: Gardi: (Rashi adds an Old French gloss.)

notes.he: כלומר הוציאו לי פתילים ממנה ואתפרנה:
notes.en: He said: Pull out threads from it for me; that is, take threads out of it for me and I will sew it.

messages.text: With what does one harvest a field of knives?

notes.he: ערוגה דסכיני במה קוצרין אותה:
notes.en: A field of knives, with what does one cut it: a bed of knives, with what does one harvest it?

notes.he: ערוגה של סכינין:
notes.en: A field of knives: a bed of knives.

messages.text: With the horn of a donkey.
But is there such an item as a horn of a donkey?
But is there such a thing as a field of knives?
Which is the egg of a black hen and which is the egg of a white hen?
messages.lead: They brought him two eggs and said to him:

notes.he: תרנגולת:
notes.en: Zagta: a hen.

messages.text: Which is the cheese from the black goat and which is from the white goat?
messages.lead: Rabbi Yehoshua brought them two cheeses, and said to them:

messages.text: And in the case of a chick that dies inside the egg, from where does its spirit exit?

notes.he: אפרוח שמת בקליפתו:
notes.en: And a chick that died: a chick that died in its shell.

notes.he: אפרוח שמת בתוך ביצתו:
notes.en: And a chick: a chick that died inside its egg.

messages.text: From where it enters, it departs.
Show us a utensil that is not worth the damage that it causes.

notes.dh: אחוי לן מנא דלא שוי חבליה
notes.he: הראנו כלי שאינו שוה ההפסד שהוא מפסיד:
notes.en: Show us a utensil that is not worth its damage: show us a utensil that is not worth the loss it causes.

notes.dh: אחוי לן מאנא דלא שוי חביליה
notes.he: כלומר הראה לנו כלי שאינו שוה ההפסד שהוא עושה:
notes.en: Show us a utensil that is not worth its damage: that is, show us a utensil that is not worth the loss it causes.

messages.text: Each one of you bring a mat and spread it out.

notes.he: מחצלת:
notes.en: Budya: a mat.

messages.text: When they did so, each mat did not enter the gate due to its size.

notes.he: שהיה ארוך ורחב יותר מן הפתח:
notes.en: It did not enter the gate: for it was longer and wider than the entrance.

notes.he: אייתי בודיא הביא מחצלת ופשטה ולא היתה יכולה ליכנס בפתח כשהיא פשוטה:
notes.en: He brought a mat and spread it out, and when spread out it could not go in through the entrance.

messages.text: Bring axes and break the gate so that you can bring it inside. This is a utensil that is not worth its damage.

notes.he: פשויי"ר בלע"ז:
notes.en: Bring axes: (Rashi adds an Old French gloss.)

notes.he: פתח הבנין והכותל עד שיכנס:
notes.en: And break it: the entrance of the building and the wall, until it goes in.

notes.he: אמר להו אייתו מרי וחציני וסתרו לבבא כדי שתהא יכולה לצאת בו אמר היינו מנא כו':
notes.en: He said to them: Bring axes and hatchets and break down the gateway, so that it can go out through it. He said: This is the utensil, etc.

messages.text: § After Rabbi Yehoshua defeated the sages of Athens in debate, he brought them to his ship as they had agreed. He then brought each one to a different room.

notes.he: למיעל בספינתא הואיל וזכינהו. היה מביאם אחד אחד בפני עצמו ומכניסו לחדר:
notes.en: He brought them: to go onto the ship, since he had defeated them. He brought them one by one, each by himself, and put each into a room.

notes.he: הרי החזיר להם תשובה כל ששאלוהו ונצחם ואייתינהו לספינתא כל חד וחד בביתיה:
notes.en: He answered them everything they asked him and defeated them, and brought them onto the ship, each one in his own room.

messages.text: All of my colleagues are coming here.
messages.lead: When each one saw the sixty mattresses in his room, he said to himself:

notes.he: סבר כל חבירי יבואו כאן:
notes.en: And when he saw sixty bistarkei: he thought, all my colleagues will come here.

messages.text: And so each waited for them without attempting to leave.
Release your ship, i.e., begin sailing.

notes.he: רבי יהושע:
notes.en: He said to him: Rabbi Yehoshua.

notes.he: רב החובל:
notes.en: To the sailor: the ship’s captain.

notes.he: התר ספינתך ולך:
notes.en: Release your ship: untie your ship and go.

messages.text: While they were coming to the emperor in Rome, he took out some dirt that he had taken from the dirt of Athens.
The story continues on 9a: at the House of the Swallowed, Rabbi Yehoshua fills a jug with its water, and then he brings the elders before the emperor.
